item.title: Socialist ends by market means: A history
item.description:

item.title: Noninvasive imaging could replace finger pricks for measuring blood glucose
item.description:
Noninvasive glucose measurementWhile most diabetes patients measure their blood glucose levels by drawing blood and testing it with a glucometer, some use wearable monitors, which have a sensor that is inserted just under the skin. In 2010, researchers at the LBRC showed that they could indirectly calculate glucose levels based on a comparison between Raman signals from the interstitial fluid that bathes skin cells and a reference measurement of blood glucose levels. More recently, the researchers reported a breakthrough that allowed them to directly measure glucose Raman signals from the skin.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 2 Comments:

analog31:

I've worked in this business. Non-invasive blood glucose monitoring has been a holy grail of analytical science for 50+ years. I've known two people who have gone bankrupt trying to do it.

The spectrum contains signatures of hundreds of compounds. All of the variation has to be accounted for. It's actually a ridiculously hard problem.

Still, holy grails being what they are, I'm still excited when I see that someone is giving it another chance.

zacian:

Having a diabetic father, who has been using pricks for the last 20 years. This would be really amazing to see this work. And I hope this can provide 24 hour glucose monitoring to see the fluctuations.
